observations.statement: All old self.stage calls were parameterless and outside mutation/patch control contexts. Direct tests stage before mutation; the three baseline tests stage through unchanged run_baseline/frozen_envelope before archive, fact, or runtime monkeypatch mutations. The selected graph is always the same v1.1 source_closure/include_conformance closure. The legacy manifest and downgrade staging calls remain independent and unchanged.

setUp still creates a fresh temp root and runs configured_fixture, then creates new SyntheticCredential and SyntheticTransport objects. copytree uses normal file copies, not links; all test archive mutations address self.root, not the template root. stage returns a copied flat reference dictionary containing only path and sha256 strings. No mutable provider, request list or resolution counter is shared.

stage_provider_binding archive refs are portable destination-relative paths. configured_fixture writes the same root-relative binding-input/profile.json pin from registry/config mappings per case. Template and case use the same component classes and source-closing options. Copied graph bytes are consumed through real manifest read, source checks and actual provider/runtime verification.

The _components module cache is pre-existing. In the reviewed graph class, runtime patch.object changes are context-managed and restored; fresh-process replay mutations stay in a subprocess, and on-disk mutations stay inside each case temp root. No reviewed case writes class reference or template files. setUpClass/addClassCleanup scopes the immutable file template to its class.

write_profile_conformance_report first binds detached to the actual verify_profile_conformance_report result, then serializes detached and writes it unchanged. The retained json.loads(output.read_bytes()) == report assertion therefore still asserts successful verifier return equality with the input report. Writer verification and schema/source binding have not been mocked. Independent positive verify equality for the stopped report and both fresh-attempt reports remains, as do five tamper rejection branches.

Moving production staging to setUpClass means staging failure is now class-setup failure rather than repeated per-case staging. Full passing counts and adjacent-class/runtime restoration must be checked dynamically before accepting performance evidence; no failed or skipped run establishes improvement.
